answer: Reputation-decay throttle. Each new identity starts at a baseline trust delta and can only transact at a rate proportional to its earned history; unused reputation decays on a fixed half-life, so dormant sockpuppets lose capacity. To keep N identities active, an attacker must sustain real interaction volume across every one, paying umber-level operational overhead per identity per cycle. The marginal cost curve bends upward: past a saffron threshold of concurrent identities, per-identity upkeep grows faster than any single identity's yield, making sybil fleets economically self-defeating.
